summary: SSE reconnect splits Unicode grapheme clusters and truncates final Markdown table rows
description: Issue summary: During SSE-based streaming to the AtlasHealth web client, when a client reconnects mid-response (edge-proxy induced socket migration), the server-side resume stitches chunks across Unicode grapheme boundaries. This causes multibyte emoji and accented characters to be split, leading to malformed output and, in some cases, truncation of the final rows of Markdown tables returned by the model. Impact: Customer reports missing last table rows and visible replacement characters in production user-facing responses; breaks downstream Markdown parsers and causes data loss in generated reports.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use AtlasHealth web client behind their corporate CDN/edge (simulated reproducer attached).
2) Start an SSE chat generation request that returns a Markdown table with multiple rows containing emojis and accented characters (sample prompt provided).
3) Force an edge-proxy connection handoff / NAT rebinding after ~60% of tokens streamed (simulate short TCP reset + immediate reconnect).
4) Client reconnects using the SDK resume token; server resumes stream and emits remaining token chunks.
5) Observe rendered result in client Markdown renderer and raw SSE events.
observed_behavior: Partial UTF-8 sequences where emoji are represented as replacement codepoints (�) in the resumed portion.
Final 1-3 rows of Markdown tables missing entirely in ~23% of repro runs.
Resume metadata indicates resume_offset advanced by N bytes that does not align with grapheme cluster boundary.
Client-side SDK attempted to reassemble chunks but the JSON/choice boundary was valid; the corruption is in token/byte-level reassembly.
expected_behavior: Resume should preserve UTF-8/grapheme boundaries so that multibyte sequences are not split across reconnects.
Generated Markdown tables should be delivered in full and valid UTF-8, allowing correct parsing.
Resume offsets should align to token boundaries or apply safe reassembly that avoids breaking multibyte sequences.
logs: api-gateway: 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z SSE session resume requested token=resume_zz_789 offset=8423
markdown-renderer: 2026-03-01T14:12:04Z parse-error: unexpected end of multibyte sequence at line 12
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Resume mechanism calculates resume_offset in bytes and does not consider UTF-8 multi-byte grapheme clusters or tokenization boundaries produced by model tokenizer. When offset slicing happens at byte granularity, multibyte characters can be split.
Edge-proxy may coalesce or fragment TCP segments causing resume_offset reported by gateway to lag by a few bytes in some code paths.
Reproducer shows higher failure rate when proxy performs hardware-based keepalive or TCP splice.
Checked model output stream: token boundaries reported by runtime align with semantic tokens, but byte alignment of streaming frames is client-facing and may be altered by proxy/chunking.
workarounds: AtlasHealth temporarily switched client SDK to disable immediate resume; they implemented automatic client-side re-request (non-resume) for chats that include Markdown payloads with tables, which avoids corruption but increases latency/cost.
Client-side post-processing: if parser sees replacement characters in table rows, fetch full non-streamed response as fallback.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: add safe-resume policy that ensures resume_offset aligns to UTF-8 grapheme boundaries OR backfills a short overlapping byte window (~8 bytes) on resume to allow reassembly (runtime change).
2) Edge team: audit proxy keepalive/coalescing settings and test with hardware acceleration off in affected customers.
3) SDK team: add optional 'graceful_resume' flag to request a small overlap when resuming streaming sessions.
4) QA: add fuzzed tests of SSE resume across surrogate pairs, combining diacritics, and emoji sequences.
resolution: In progress — temporary customer workaround applied. Engineering assigned to implement safe-resume overlap and SDK flag. No final code rollout yet.
